==Problem==
The figure below shows a large white circle with a number of smaller white and shaded circles in its
interior. What fraction of the interior of the large white circle is shaded?

<asy>
// Diagram by TheMathGuyd
size(6cm);
draw(circle((3,3),3));
filldraw(circle((2,3),2),lightgrey);
filldraw(circle((3,3),1),white);
filldraw(circle((1,3),1),white);
filldraw(circle((5.5,3),0.5),lightgrey);
filldraw(circle((4.5,4.5),0.5),lightgrey);
filldraw(circle((4.5,1.5),0.5),lightgrey);
int i, j;
for(i=0; i<7; i=i+1)
{
draw((0,i)--(6,i), dashed+grey);
draw((i,0)--(i,6), dashed+grey);
}
</asy>


<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ \frac{1}{4} \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ \frac{11}{36} \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ \frac{1}{3} \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ \frac{19}{36} \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ \frac{5}{9}</imath>

==Solution 1==
First, the total area of the radius <imath>3</imath> circle is simply just <imath>9\cdot \pi</imath> when using our area of a circle formula. 

Now from here, we have to find our shaded area. This can be done by adding the areas of the <imath>\frac{1}{2}</imath>-radius circles and add; then, take the area of the <imath>1</imath> radius circles and subtract that from the area of the <imath>2</imath> radius circle to get our resulting complex shape area. Adding these up, we will get <imath>3\cdot \frac{1}{4} \pi + 4 \pi -\pi - \pi = \frac{3}{4} \pi + 2 \pi = \frac{11\cdot \pi}{4}</imath>.

So, our answer is <imath>\frac {\frac{11}{4} \pi}{9 \pi} = \boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ \frac{11}{36}}</imath>.

==Solution 2==

Pretend each circle is a square. The large shaded circle is a square with area <imath>16~\text{units}^2</imath>, and the two white circles inside it each have areas of <imath>4~\text{units}^2</imath>, which adds up to <imath>8~\text{units}^2</imath>. The three small shaded circles become three squares with area <imath>1~\text{units}^2</imath>, and add up to <imath>3~\text{units}^2</imath>. Adding the areas of the shaded circles (19) and subtracting the areas of the white circles (8), we get <imath>11~\text{units}^2</imath>. Since the largest white circle in which all these other circles are becomes a square that has area <imath>36~\text{units}^2</imath>, our answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ \dfrac{11}{36}}</imath>.

-yume_mita
